q: What is the recommended circulation space between low height objects in a living room?
n: Reference: Max Fajardo’s Planning Handbook. It says 40-45cm clearance between low height objects. Low objects such as a sofa and coffee table need about 400–450 mm of clear space between them. Source: Fajardo, Planning and Designing Handbook (Living Room); Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space.

q: What is the recommended counter space on the sides of a range in a kitchen counter?
n: Kitchen planning guides recommend landing counter space beside a cooking surface. About 30–60 cm on the sides makes 55 cm a comfortable allowance. Source: NKBA Kitchen Planning Guidelines (Cooking Surface Landing Area); Time-Saver Standards for Housing.

q: What is the comfortable reach for a kitchen counter without squatting?
n: Kitchen storage is most comfortable to reach between about 600 mm and 1,700 mm above the floor. Below about 600 mm the user must stoop or squat. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space (Kitchen Reach Zones); Neufert, Architects' Data.

q: A G-shaped kitchen layout is also known as what?
n: A G-shaped kitchen is a U-shaped kitchen with a peninsula forming a partial fourth side, so it is also called a peninsula kitchen. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Housing and Residential Development (Kitchen Layouts); NKBA Kitchen Planning Guidelines.

q: The size of the TV screen is measured
n: A TV or monitor is specified by its screen diagonal, from corner to corner. Source: Consumer Electronics (CTA) display sizing convention; Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space.

q: What is the maximum slope for permanent excavation and fills?
n: Permanent excavation and fill slopes are commonly limited to 1 vertical to 2 horizontal unless a soils investigation justifies steeper slopes. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule on Excavation and Grading; International Building Code, Sec. 1804.

q: An unoccupied space between building lines and yard.
n: A court is an unoccupied open space bounded by building walls and lot lines (or yards). It is open to the sky and gives light and ventilation. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII, Sec. 804 and Glossary (Court).

q: Which of the following is not allowed in an R-3 zone?
n: High-rise condominiums belong in higher-density zones. R-3 is for medium density, such as townhouses, apartels and lodging houses. Source: HLURB Model Zoning Ordinance (R-3 Zone); 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII.

q: What is the maximum building height in number of storeys allowed for an R-3 (maximum) lot?
n: Maximum R-3 development has a building height limit of 12 storeys (36.00 m). Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Table VII.2 (BHL – R-3).

q: What does PUD mean in zoning?
n: PUD stands for Planned Unit Development: land developed as a single entity under one plan, with mixed uses and clustered buildings. Source: HLURB Model Zoning Ordinance (Definitions); 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Glossary.

q: What is the minimum width of the access road for a rear lot?
n: Per the exam key, a rear lot must have an access road (private way) at least 3.00 m wide to a public street. Source: PD 957 Revised IRR (Lot Access) and 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII (Access).

q: What is the minimum width of the planting strip if trees are to be planted?
n: Per the exam key, planting strips with trees should be at least 300 mm wide, wider where root space allows. Source: BP 220 / PD 957 Revised IRR (Planting Strips); NBCP Rule VIII (Sidewalks and Planting Strips).

q: What is the minimum slope of an entrance ramp?
n: There is no minimum slope of an entrance ramp but maximum. Accessibility rules set a maximum ramp gradient of 1:12, not a minimum. A ramp may be gentler, so no minimum slope is prescribed. Source: BP 344 IRR, Rule II, Minimum Requirements – Ramps; BP 344 2024 Revised IRR.

q: What is recommended for narrower sidewalks?
n: On narrow sidewalks, raised (barrier) curbs keep vehicles from mounting the walkway and protect pedestrians. Mountable curbs are used only where sidewalks are wide. Source: DPWH Design Guidelines, Criteria and Standards (Curbs and Sidewalks); PD 957 IRR.

q: What does FLAR mean?
n: FLAR means Floor-to-Lot Area Ratio: the ratio of the allowable gross floor area to the total lot area. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 707 and Table VII.G.1.

q: What is the area of the middle zone?
n: The 9,600 sqm lot minus the 3,000 sqm front zone and the 3,000 sqm rear zone leaves 3,600 sqm for the middle zone. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII (Total Lot Area).

DESIGN PROBLEM NO. 4 – BULACAN TRUCK HUB

Design Problem. A business empire wanted to venture into the trucking industry. The owner acquired several delivery trucks and vans that are to be deployed in Metro Manila. Aside from the trucking business, the owner also owns a small chain of gasoline stations all around Luzon. He proposes that the gasoline station be constructed near the trucking facility. The large lot shall be divided into three zones - one for the gasoline station, one for the trucking facility and one for the residential building.
a. The front zone measuring 3.000sqm shall be used for the gasoline station. It shall have a small service area and a convenience store measuring 50sqm.
b. The middle zone shall be for the trucking facilities. This zone shall accommodate two buildings. The first building measures 35m x 40m while the second building measures 30m x 45m.
c. The rear zone measuring 3.000sqm shall be for a mid-rise residential building. The 7-storey residential building shall have 11,200sqm TGFA. On the 3rd to 7th floor, there shall be rentable residential units, especially for the workers of the trucking facility.
d. Included on the three zones is a 6.5m wide driveway servicing all zones. The driveway runs parallel to the left of the lot.
Site Features. The proposed site is rectangular inside lot measuring 60m x 9,600sqm sloping 3% downwards towards the rear side of the lot. The 60m frontage of the lot is facing a 15m-wide national highway. The left and right sides of the lot are bounded by other privately owned lands. The rear side is bounded by another lot also owned by the business empire and is reserved for future expansion, potentially for residential purposes. The city planning department cleared the project as special zoning classification (SPE).
Design Objectives. The owner of the project hired a Bulacan-based design and construction firm. The design challenge for the project is to provide good architectural solutions considering the different uses within the lot. The different zones shall not be easily disrupted by adjacent uses.

q: According to the building code, what is the approximate GFA of the residential building?
n: Since TGFA is the only given parameter on the residential building, we will convert this into GFA. Using Table VII.G.2 column 2, we can consider the structure as residential maximum development. With that, it means that 16% of the TGFA is non-GFA. So GFA = TGFA x 0.84 = 11,200sqm x 0.84 = 9,408sqm. For a maximum-development residential building, the non-GFA allowance is 16% of TGFA. GFA = 11,200 sqm x 0.84 = 9,408 sqm. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 707 and Table VII.G.2.

q: What is the total perimeter of the lot?
n: 9,600 sqm / 60 m = 160 m deep. Perimeter = 2 x (60 m + 160 m) = 440 m. Source: Brinker & Wolf, Elementary Surveying (Lot Measurement).

q: The angle of the angular plane is measured from:
n: The angular plane that limits building height is projected from the centerline of the RROW in front of the lot. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 707 (Angular Plane) and Figure VII.20.

q: What is the minimum width of a code-compliant T&B?
n: Sec. 806 sets the minimum toilet and bath size at 1.20 sqm, with a least dimension of 0.90 m. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII, Sec. 806 (Size and Dimensions of Rooms).

q: According to the building code, what is the allowable maximum building footprint for a low density residential area?
n: Take note that since it mentioned building code, we will only rely on the building code. The design problem mentioned that while the zone is low density residential (R-1), the local zoning ordinance allows duplexes on R-1 zones. For this question, we will only consider the project as R-1 (not as duplex). For the allowable max PSO, you can refer to Table 7.1 and 8.1. From Table 7.1, the AMBF is 60% of TLA. From Table 8.1, no R-1 provision was provided except for the illustration (Figure 8.1). The figure shows that the maximum PSO shall be 50% of TLA for an R-1. Therefore, the answer is 50% of TLA. Per the exam key, low-density residential lots are given an allowable maximum building footprint of 50% of the total lot area. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Table VII.1 (R-1/Low-Density Residential – AMBF).

q: Where should the true copy of the tax declaration be requested by the owner?
n: Tax declarations, and certified true copies of them, are kept and issued by the City or Municipal Assessor's Office. Source: Local Government Code (RA 7160), Sec. 472 (Assessor) and Real Property Taxation provisions.

q: What is the mean temperature in Baguio?
n: Baguio's annual mean temperature is about 18–19°C, because of its elevation of about 1,500 m. Source: PAGASA Climatological Normals (Baguio station).

q: What is the maximum GFA allowed for the project if the local zoning ordinance dictates that the maximum floor to lot area ratio is 1.5?
n: Remember the formula for MaxGFA = TLA x maximum FLAR. Therefore, maxGFA = 342 sqm xX 1.5 = 513 sqm. Maximum GFA = TLA x maximum FLAR = 342 sqm x 1.5 = 513 sqm. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 707 (FLAR and GFA).

DESIGN PROBLEM NO. 2 – TWO-STOREY DUPLEX RESIDENTIAL

Design Problem. A successful businesswoman wanted to try to venture out in the real estate industry. She recently purchased a lot from a famous developer located in a low density residential area of Mabalacat, Pampanga. Her friend, who is an architect, was commissioned to do the residential project. The architect suggested a two-storey duplex house to accommodate two families. Upon the initial and succeeding meetings, the following space requirements were determined by the architect:
a. The two units shall have the same uniform floor area. Each unit has a paved 2- car carport where a standard 3m x 5m car slot can be accommodated. A covered porch measuring 3m x 6 sqm welcomes the guests.
b. The layout of one unit is mirrored on the other. On the ground floor, there should be a foyer, stairs leading to the next floor level, toilet and bath and a bedroom - all these spaces along the party wall. The living, dining and kitchen spaces enjoy the direct view of the side yards.
c. The second floor of each unit contains two bedrooms (one is a master bedroom) each with a walk-in closet and its own T&B. The 2nd floor plate measures 91 sqm including two 6-sqm balconies connected to each bedroom. The floor slab has a 100mm thickness made of reinforced concrete.
d. Entrance steps shall be provided from the front yard to the entrance porch.
Site Features. The purchased lot is fronting a road on one of its sides. The road runs exactly along the N-S axis. The lot parcel is bounded on the W along line 1-2 by Lot 5; on the N along line 2-3 by a community garden maintained by HOA; on the E along line 3-4 by a public RROW; and on the S along line 4-1 by Lot 7. Looking at the land title of the lot, its technical description reads from point 1; N 6°20' E, 18m to point 2; S 83°40' E, 18m to point 3; (unreadable bearings) to point 4; N 83°40' W, 20m back to point 1. The slope of the lot runs downward at 2% from North to South.
Design Objectives. The subdivision guidelines allow the use of front yards as paved carport as long as the required open space is complied. The guidelines also required lot owners to add 500mm to the minimum front setback required by the building code. All other setbacks shall follow the code. As the front lot line is oblique to the other lot lines, the front setback shall be measured from point 3 of the lot. It means that the front yard areas vary between the two units. The local zoning ordinance allows duplex structures in a low density residential zone.

q: What is an accessory structure in a memorial park?
n: A chapel is only an accessory structure in a memorial park or cemetery. All other mentioned are primary structures in this type of use. In a memorial park, a chapel is an accessory structure. Columbaria, niches and the perimeter wall serve the park's primary use. Source: PD 856 (Code on Sanitation), Ch. XXI (Disposal of Dead Persons) and DOH implementing rules; HLURB Memorial Park Rules.

q: What is the minimum width of a walkway placed in front of a parking slot?
n: Walkways in front of parking slots should be at least about 1.20 m wide, so a car's overhang does not block pedestrians. Source: BP 344 2024 Amended IRR (Walkways); 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII (Parking).

q: Where is a total station primarily used?
n: A total station measures angles and distances electronically for land surveying and layout. It is a geodetic (surveying) instrument. Source: Brinker & Wolf, Elementary Surveying; Geodetic Engineering Law (RA 8560).

q: Recommended size for perpendicular parking slot.
n: The NBC sets standard perpendicular and angled car slots at 2.50 m × 5.00 m. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 707 (Parking slot dimensions).

q: According to the code, what is the maximum FLAR allowed for the lot?
n: Per the exam key, the maximum FLAR for this commercial lot is 9. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 707 and Table VII.2 (Maximum FLAR).

DESIGN PROBLEM NO. 5 – PROPOSED MEDIUM RISE COMMERCIAL BUILDING

Design Problem. A businesswoman commissioned you to design and construct a medium-rise commercial building in Pasig City. The building spaces will be rented to different kinds of establishments. After identifying the development controls and the user requirements, you came up with the following initial plan:
a. To maximize the profitability of the lot, you determined that the maximum building footprint allowed is 1,024sqm. No firewalls were introduced.
b. The building shall have the least number of storeys to be considered as medium- rise (according to the code). The GFA shall be 8,000sqm.
c. Underground parking shall be provided and the ground floor shall be reserved for a small supermarket or a fastfood chain. The upper floors shall accommodate other commercial establishments.
Site Features. The lot for this project is bounded on its two adjacent sides by roads - one with 20m width and the other with 15m width. The wider road runs along the east- west axis while the other runs along the north-south axis. The site measures 40m facing the wider road and has a total of 1,600sqm area. The north side of the lot is bounded by another undeveloped commercial lot while the west side is bounded by an existing commercial building with a maximized footprint (with firewall). The property slopes 2% downward towards the existing adjacent building. The area is zoned as medium intensity commercial area.
Design Objectives. Since the commercial building is open to any kind of establishments, you are challenged to create a building design and plans with flexibility in layout. The building facade shall also maximize its good orientation, having two frontages.

s: Design Problem 5 – Proposed Medium Rise Commercial Building
q: What is the proposed FLAR for the project?
n: Proposed FLAR = GFA / TLA = 8,000 sqm / 1,600 sqm = 5. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 707 (FLAR).

q: In anthropometrics and average body proportions, the height of a human is roughly equal to __ times of its head height?
n: In classical proportion studies, an adult's height is about 7.5 to 8 head heights. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space; Neufert, Architects' Data (Human Proportions).

q: Custodial closets shall be placed near which building space?
n: Custodial closet is just another name for janitorial closet. Janitor's (custodial) closets are put next to comfort rooms. They need a slop sink and water supply and mainly serve toilet cleaning. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Building Types (Office Buildings – Support Spaces); Neufert, Architects' Data.

q: A concealed cistern is most commonly used for which plumbing fixture?
n: A concealed (in-wall) cistern goes with wall-hung water closets. The tank sits inside the wall frame, and only the flush plate shows. Source: Manufacturers' installation guides (in-wall carrier systems); Revised National Plumbing Code.

q: What is the ideal dimensions of a breastfeeding cubicle?
n: A lactation station needs enough space for a seat, a small table, a sink nearby and privacy. About 2.0 m × 2.0 m is a common minimum. Source: RA 10028 (Expanded Breastfeeding Promotion Act) and its IRR (Lactation Station standards).

q: A structured cabling system is provided to support what?
n: A structured cabling system is a complete system of cabling and associated hardware, which provides a comprehensive telecommunications infrastructure. This infrastructure serves a wide range of uses, such as to provide telephone service or transmit data through a computer network. Structured cabling is a standardized cabling system that supports data and communications: voice, data and video networks. Source: TIA-568 (Commercial Building Telecommunications Cabling); ISO/IEC 11801.

q: What is the ideal kitchen space for the canteen, considering the standard ratio of kitchen to dining space?
n: The area of the canteen is 126 sqm. The standard ratio is 60% dining space and 40% kitchen space. Therefore, the ideal kitchen area is 126 sqm x 0.4 = 50.4 sqm. At the usual 60:40 split of dining to kitchen, kitchen = 126 sqm x 0.40 = 50.4 sqm. Source: Neufert, Architects' Data (Restaurants and Canteens); Time-Saver Standards for Building Types (Food Service).

DESIGN PROBLEM NO. 1 – SEVEN-STOREY GOVERNMENT OFFICE

Design Problem: The Local Government of Quezon City is planning to add a seven-storey civic center building in its City Hall Compound. This building will house several business departments catering the public. The city government allocates 2,400 sqm lot for this new building. The following spaces shall be accommodated in the planning:
a. The ground floor shall have a 25m x 30m covered parking on the SE side of the lot. This side of the building is where the exit discharge of the building is located. The exit discharge runs along the side yard of the lot to the public RROW. On the right side (when facing the lot), the lobby which measures 25m x 500sqm accommodates the waiting customers of the releasing office. The releasing office measuring 11m x 10m is located at the back of the building along the stairs, elevator and comfort rooms. The stairs and elevator have a combined area of 90sqm and located between the releasing office and the comfort room. The comfort room is measuring 5m wide and 10m long.
b. The comfort room, stairs and elevator areas are in the same size and location on the 2nd to 7th floor of the building. A 50m long and 2m wide corridor is running along the long side of the building. The comfort room, stair and elevator area is connected to this corridor. The corridor divides the floor into two offices - one large measuring 43m x 18m and one smaller office measuring 36m x 10m. A canteen is accessible on one end of the corridor which measures 7m x 126sqm. This layout is almost the same on the 3rd until 7th floor except that the areas of the canteen and large office are combined and divided equally. The 3rd to 7th floor has 3 offices - one measuring 360sqm and two measuring 450sqm. The rooftop of the building is not accessible to the public but can be used for mechanical and plumbing accessory rooms.
c. Half of the 7m-wide front yard shall be softscapes usable by the public. 10% of the parking shall have softscapes for better indoor air quality. Side setbacks measure 5m while rear setback is only 3m.
Site Features. The site is a regular lot fronting a road that connects East Avenue and Kalayaan Avenue. The road is named Makatarungan and has a 5m carriageway with 1.5m sidewalk on both sides. The longer front side of the lot is oriented 72° from North to West. This front side measures 60m. The slope of the lot is generally flat.
Design Objectives. Good circulation is a major consideration for the design since this is a public building. Within the offices, proper planning shall be done to accommodate the requirements of each office or department. Take note that each department has workflows which shall be the basis of the space plan. No waiting areas shall be located on the corridor. All waiting areas shall be within offices.

q: What is the ideal dining space for the canteen?
n: At the same 60:40 split, dining = 126 sqm x 0.60 = 75.6 sqm. Source: Neufert, Architects' Data (Restaurants and Canteens); Time-Saver Standards for Building Types (Food Service).

q: What is the length of the corridor on each floor?

Design Objectives. Good circulation is a major consideration for the design since this is a public building. Within the offices, proper planning shall be done to accommodate the requirements of each office or department. Take note that each department has workflows which shall be the basis of the space plan. No waiting areas shall be located on the corridor. All waiting areas shall be within offices.

q: Which of the following is not part of GFA?
n: The NBC excludes covered parking from the gross floor area. Corridors, circulation and offices are included. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 707 (GFA definition and exclusions).

q: What is the primary determinant of building bulk?
n: FLAR (floor-to-lot area ratio) is the main control on building bulk because it caps the gross floor area allowed on a lot. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 707 (FLAR).

q: In a visual field, which of the following are the negative elements?
n: In figure-ground perception the background is the negative (ground) element, and figures or objects are the positive elements. Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space and Order (Figure-Ground).

q: In terms of acoustics, what material is not ideal for the interior cladding of a noisy space?
n: For noisy spaces, absorptive or diffusive materials are more appropriate. Among these choices, mirror finish walls only reflect sound. Therefore, it is the least ideal. Hard, smooth, mirror-finish walls reflect almost all sound and add to reverberation. Noisy spaces need absorptive or diffusive cladding. Source: Egan, Architectural Acoustics (Absorption and Reflection); Long, Architectural Acoustics.

q: What is not an ideal exterior color for a firewall?
n: Although the color does not really affect the functionality of a firewall in terms of fire protection, its color affects the heat gain of the building. Black absorbs light energy and therefore must be avoided to prevent excessive heating of the wall that can penetrate the building interior. A black firewall absorbs the most solar heat, which raises cooling loads and thermal stress. Light colors reflect sunlight. Source: Lechner, Heating, Cooling, Lighting (Surface Color and Solar Absorptance); Philippine Green Building Code (2015).

q: Which is not included in architectural interiors?
n: Per the exam key, "fittings" are excluded from architectural interiors because they are treated as building hardware and services. Note: item 127 is keyed differently. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3 (Architectural Interiors); Architect's Guidelines (2016), Sec. 7.3.

q: What is the minimum width of an accessible corridor?
n: Among the choices, 1.20 m is the minimum accessible corridor width under the original BP 344 IRR. The 2024 amended IRR raises corridors to 1.50 m. Source: BP 344 IRR, Rule II – Corridors; BP 344 2024 Amended IRR, Corridors, item 5.1.

q: Which of the following is not considered casework?
n: Casework is built-in cabinetry such as cabinets, drawers and shelving racks. A table is loose furniture. Source: Architectural Woodwork Standards (AWI, Casework); Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction.

q: Which is not a millwork?
n: Millwork is mill-made woodwork such as doors, moldings and trims. Hinges are hardware. Source: Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction (Millwork); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 10.

q: Which of the following is a furnishing?
n: Furnishings are movable items and accessories that equip and adorn an interior, including art such as sculpture. Playground equipment, vending machines and saunas are equipment. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Furnishings).

q: A heavy curtain.
n: Drapes (draperies) are heavy, often lined curtains that hang in folds. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Window Treatments).

q: A table ideal for the hallway.
n: Console tables are usually slender, long tables that people place in their entryway or hallway. Its height is usually the same as regular table. A console table is a narrow table placed against a wall. It is ideal for hallways and foyers. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Furniture); Time-Saver Standards for Interior Design.
